name: Horseshoe (flap) retinal tear
definition: A full-thickness retinal break with a flap of retina still attached to vitreous at its anterior margin, produced by vitreoretinal traction (usually during posterior vitreous detachment) at the posterior border of the vitreous base or at a focal vitreoretinal adhesion.

location.notes: Most occur in the equatorial zone at the posterior border of the vitreous base (juxtabasal), between equator and ora; autopsy series show all quadrants, clinically superior/temporal quadrants predominate; frequently at margins of lattice or cystic tufts.

drawing.description: Draw a U/horseshoe-shaped area filled red with a blue outline, rounded apex pointing posteriorly (toward the disc) and open horns pointing anteriorly toward the ora; draw the anterior flap as a curved blue line at the base. Add surrounding blue if subretinal fluid is present.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break: blue outline filled red); Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (rolled flap edges as curved blue lines)

Natural history of retinal breaks without detachment.

name: Operculated retinal hole (round hole with free operculum)
definition: A round full-thickness retinal break whose plug of retina (operculum) has been completely avulsed by vitreous traction and floats free in the vitreous above the hole, relieving traction on the hole margin.

location.notes: Between equator and ora; operculum lies in the detached vitreous just anterior to (in front of) the hole; extrabasal holes may arise from avulsed cystic tufts.

drawing.description: Draw a small round red-filled circle with a blue outline; draw the free operculum as a small green-filled shape just beside the hole (displaced slightly toward the centre of the chart to indicate it floats in the vitreous).

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break); Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (retinal operculum drawn green)

pubmed.title: Retinal breaks without detachment: natural history, management and long term follow-up.
Tears of the peripheral retina; pathogenesis, incidence and classification in autopsy eyes.
Natural history of retinal breaks without detachment.

name: Atrophic round hole
definition: A small round full-thickness retinal break of trophic (atrophic) origin without a flap or operculum, most often arising within lattice degeneration and not caused by acute vitreous traction.

location.notes: Between equator and ora, frequently within or at the edge of lattice degeneration; primary (non-lattice) holes are usually single, within the vitreous base zone, in elderly eyes.

drawing.description: Draw a small round circle filled red with a blue outline; if inside lattice, place it within the lattice band. Surround with a blue ring if a cuff of subretinal fluid is present.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break: blue outline filled red)

pubmed.title: Retinal holes.
Long-term natural history of lattice degeneration of the retina.

name: Giant retinal tear
definition: A full-thickness neurosensory retinal break extending circumferentially for 90° (3 clock hours) or more in the presence of a posteriorly detached vitreous.

location.notes: Circumferential, at or just posterior to the posterior border of the vitreous base (between ora and equator); the posterior retinal flap may fold over (invert) when detached. Associated with high myopia, trauma, Stickler syndrome.

drawing.description: Draw a circumferential crescent filled red with a blue outline spanning ≥3 clock hours between equator and ora; draw the posterior flap edge as a curved blue line (folded/inverted edge drawn as a double blue line). Detached retina posterior to it is filled blue.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break); note: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology alternatively cross-lines the open area in red, but CMS reserves red cross-hatch for partial-thickness breaks

name: Retinal dialysis (oral disinsertion)
definition: A circumferential full-thickness break at the ora serrata in which the retina is disinserted from the non-pigmented epithelium of the pars plana, with vitreous typically remaining attached to the posterior edge of the break.

location.notes: Located exactly at the ora serrata; inferotemporal most common (spontaneous/young patients); superonasal classically after blunt trauma; may be multiple or bilateral.

drawing.description: Draw a thin circumferential band filled red with a blue outline whose anterior edge lies on the ora serrata circle; if retina adjacent to the ora is detached, also draw the black scalloped line over the ora circle and fill the detachment blue.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break; black scalloped ora line for adjacent detached retina)

name: Avulsion of the vitreous base
definition: Traumatic tearing of the vitreous base away from its insertion, producing a ribbon ('bucket handle') of non-pigmented ciliary epithelium and/or peripheral retina suspended in the vitreous; pathognomonic of blunt ocular trauma and often associated with dialysis.

location.notes: Straddles the ora serrata / pars plana; strip hangs into the anterior vitreous; frequently accompanies traumatic dialysis or large oral tears (temporal or superonasal).

drawing.description: Draw a curved green ribbon parallel to and straddling the ora/pars plana circles to represent the avulsed vitreous base in the vitreous; draw any accompanying dialysis or tear beneath it with break colours (blue outline, red fill).

color_source: inferred: CMS green = opacities in media (suspended tissue in vitreous)

name: Tear of the pars plana non-pigmented epithelium
definition: A traumatic break limited to the non-pigmented epithelium of the pars plana ciliaris anterior to the ora, which can cause a shallow rhegmatogenous retinal detachment despite no retinal break being present.

location.notes: In the band between ora and ciliary processes; requires scleral depression to see; associated with closed-globe contusion; detachment may present months later.

typical_size: small, a fraction of a clock hour

drawing.description: Draw a small red-filled, blue-outlined break inside the pars plana band (between the ora and outer ciliary-process circles); fill any associated detached retina blue.

color_source: inferred: CMS full-thickness break rule (blue outline filled red) applied to the pars plana epithelium

pubmed.title: Retinal detachments due to traumatic tears in the pars plana ciliaris.

name: Full-thickness macular hole
definition: A foveal lesion with interruption of all neural retinal layers from the internal limiting membrane to the retinal pigment epithelium, seen ophthalmoscopically as a round red punched-out defect often with a grey cuff of subretinal fluid and sometimes an overlying (pseudo)operculum.

location.notes: Centred on the fovea; cuff of subretinal fluid around the hole; yellow deposits may be seen at the base; prehole opacity/(pseudo)operculum may lie on the posterior hyaloid.

typical_size: ≈1/8–1/3 disc diameter (IVTS: small ≤250 µm, medium >250–400 µm, large >400 µm)

drawing.description: Draw a small round red-filled circle with a blue outline at the fovea; add a thin blue ring for the cuff of subretinal fluid and a small green dot just off-centre for an operculum/pseudo-operculum if present.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break; blue = detached retina); Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (operculum green)

name: Lamellar macular hole
definition: A partial-thickness foveal defect with irregular foveal contour, undermined edges and apparent loss of foveal tissue, seen ophthalmoscopically as a round reddish foveal lesion with intact outer retina.

location.notes: Centred on the fovea; often with epiretinal proliferation/membrane; diagnosis confirmed by OCT but lesion is visible and charted clinically.

drawing.description: Draw a small round blue outline at the fovea and cross-hatch its interior in red to indicate a partial-thickness break.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (partial-thickness sensory retinal break: blue outline cross-hatched red)

pubmed.title: Optical coherence tomography-based consensus definition for lamellar macular hole.
Surgical interventions for lamellar macular holes.

name: Partial-thickness retinal break
definition: A retinal break that involves only part of the neurosensory retinal thickness (e.g., inner-layer hole of retinoschisis, lamellar hole, deep erosion), so that no direct communication exists between vitreous and subretinal space.

location.notes: Most often peripheral (within lattice, at the vitreous base or in the inner wall of retinoschisis); at the fovea it is charted as a lamellar macular hole.

drawing.description: Draw the outline of the defect in blue and cross-hatch its interior in red.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (partial-thickness sensory retinal break: blue outline cross-hatched red)

pubmed.title: Monitoring retinoschisis and non-acute retinal detachment by optical coherence tomography: morphologic aspects and clinical impact.
Optical coherence tomography-based consensus definition for lamellar macular hole.
Optical coherence tomography features of lattice degeneration.

name: Retinal erosion / localized retinal thinning
definition: A sharply demarcated, reddish area of inner neurosensory retinal thinning without a full-thickness defect, typically within lattice degeneration or near the vitreous base, which may later evolve into an atrophic hole.

location.notes: Between equator and ora, commonly in the floor of lattice lesions; looks redder than surrounding retina because the retina is thin.

drawing.description: Draw a blue outline around the thin area and cross-hatch the interior in red (same symbol as a partial-thickness break).

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (partial-thickness break: blue outline cross-hatched red); Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (thin retinal areas: blue outline, red cross-lines)

pubmed.title: Optical coherence tomography features of lattice degeneration.
Ultra-Widefield Steering-Based Spectral-Domain Optical Coherence Tomography Imaging of the Retinal Periphery.

name: Inner-layer hole in retinoschisis
definition: A break confined to the thin inner wall of a retinoschisis cavity; small and round in degenerative retinoschisis, but may be very large in X-linked retinoschisis, leaving vessels bridging the defect.

location.notes: Located on the inner (vitreous-facing) wall of the schisis cavity; by itself does not cause retinal detachment.

typical_size: small (1/10–1/2 DD) in degenerative schisis; up to several clock hours in XLRS

drawing.description: Draw a blue outline within the blue-hatched schisis area and cross-hatch the open portion in red.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (open portion of inner-layer holes red cross-lined, blue outline); Requisites for Fundus drawing (SlideShare) https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retina-drwaing/163697941; CMS L33567 App A (partial-thickness break)

name: Outer-layer hole in retinoschisis
definition: A break in the outer wall of a retinoschisis cavity, typically larger, round with rolled edges and posterior to the equator, through which schisis fluid can enter the subretinal space to produce a schisis-detachment.

location.notes: Within the area of schisis, often near its posterior border and posterior to the equator; seen best with scleral depression/retro-illumination.

drawing.description: Draw a round red-filled area with a blue outline inside the blue-hatched schisis region; fill any surrounding subretinal fluid blue.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (open interior of outer-layer holes red, blue outline); Requisites for Fundus drawing (SlideShare) https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retina-drwaing/163697941; CMS L33567 App A (full-thickness break colours)

name: Retinal break with cuff of subretinal fluid
definition: A retinal break surrounded by a small localized rim of subretinal fluid that does not extend more than about 1–2 disc diameters from the break (subclinical retinal detachment).

location.notes: Around atrophic holes or tears between equator and ora; usually asymptomatic and slowly progressive or stable.

typical_size: break plus a 1/4–2 disc diameter rim of fluid

drawing.description: Draw the break as red with a blue outline and surround it with a blue-shaded ring representing the detached retina of the cuff.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (break: blue outline filled red; blue = detached retina)

pubmed.title: Subclinical retinal detachment resulting from asymptomatic retinal breaks: prognosis for progression and regression.

name: Bridging vessel across a retinal tear
definition: A retinal blood vessel that remains intact across a retinal tear, attached to the vitreous-borne flap, and can bleed into the vitreous with ongoing traction.

location.notes: Crosses the open area of a horseshoe tear from posterior retina to the flap.

drawing.description: Draw the tear with break colours, then a red line (artery; blue if a vein) running across the red-filled tear to its flap.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (red = retinal arteries, blue = retinal veins)

pubmed.title: Retinal breaks without detachment: natural history, management and long term follow-up.

name: Lattice degeneration
definition: A circumferentially oriented, sharply demarcated spindle-shaped area of peripheral retinal thinning with overlying vitreous liquefaction and firm vitreoretinal adhesion at its margins, often showing white sclerotic vessels, pigment and small atrophic holes.

location.notes: Between equator and ora (anterior to equator), circumferential, often in the vertical meridians (superior > inferior, temporal > nasal); may lie in parallel rows; frequently bilateral; associated with myopia.

typical_size: fraction of a clock hour to ~3 clock hours long; ~1/4–1 DD wide

drawing.description: Draw an elongated circumferential spindle with a black outline and fill it with a black lattice (criss-cross 'X') pattern, oriented parallel to the ora.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (black outline filled with black lattice pattern = lattice in attached retina)

name: Lattice degeneration with atrophic holes
definition: Lattice degeneration containing one or more small round atrophic full-thickness holes within its thinned floor.

location.notes: Holes lie inside the lattice band between equator and ora; subclinical detachment may develop around them.

drawing.description: Draw the lattice symbol (black outline + black lattice pattern) and place small red-filled, blue-outlined circles inside it for each hole.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (lattice symbol + full-thickness break symbol)

pubmed.title: Long-term natural history of lattice degeneration of the retina.
Retinal holes.
Optical coherence tomography features of lattice degeneration.

name: Lattice degeneration with tractional (flap) tear
synonyms: tear at posterior margin of lattice
definition: Lattice degeneration with a flap tear at its posterior or lateral margin, created by vitreous traction on the firm vitreoretinal adhesion at the lattice border during posterior vitreous detachment.

location.notes: Tear arises at the posterior (or end) margin of the lattice band where vitreous is adherent.

drawing.description: Draw the lattice symbol (black outline + black lattice pattern) and a horseshoe tear (red fill, blue outline) at its posterior edge with the tear apex pointing posteriorly.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (lattice symbol + full-thickness break symbol)

pubmed.title: Long-term natural history of lattice degeneration of the retina.

name: Pigmented lattice degeneration
definition: Lattice degeneration in which the thinned area contains prominent clumps of hyperpigmentation from RPE migration, with or without the classic white sclerotic vessels.

location.notes: Same distribution as lattice: circumferential between equator and ora.

typical_size: fraction of a clock hour to ~3 clock hours

drawing.description: Draw the lattice symbol (black outline + black lattice pattern) and add extra black dots/clumps within it to indicate the pigment.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (lattice of attached retina: black outline, black lattice pattern)

pubmed.title: Lattice degeneration of the retina.
Optical coherence tomography features of lattice degeneration.

name: Lattice degeneration in detached retina
definition: Lattice degeneration located within an area of detached retina.

location.notes: Between equator and ora, inside the detached (blue) area.

typical_size: fraction of a clock hour to ~3 clock hours

drawing.description: Draw an elongated circumferential spindle with a blue outline filled with a blue lattice (criss-cross) pattern.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (blue outline filled with blue lattice pattern = lattice of detached retina)

pubmed.title: Lattice degeneration of the retina.

name: Radial perivascular lattice degeneration
definition: Lattice-like retinal thinning and pigmentation oriented radially along retinal vessels, typically posterior to the equator, characteristic of Stickler and related hereditary vitreoretinopathies.

location.notes: Radial bands following major retinal vessels from the equator posteriorly; often multiple and bilateral.

drawing.description: Draw radially oriented spindles along the vessels with a black outline and black lattice pattern.

color_source: inferred: CMS lattice rule (black outline + black lattice pattern)

name: Snail-track degeneration
definition: A sharply demarcated, elongated band of glistening white frost-like ('snowflake') dots in the peripheral retina without the white sclerotic vessels of classic lattice, considered a variant or early stage of lattice degeneration.

location.notes: Circumferential bands between equator and ora, often in myopic eyes; may contain atrophic holes.

typical_size: 1–3 clock hours; band up to ~1 DD wide

drawing.description: Draw a circumferential band with a black (lattice-type) outline filled with fine green stippling for the frost-like snowflakes.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (green stipple = frosting/snowflakes on lattice); outline inferred from CMS lattice rule (black)

name: White without pressure
definition: A translucent grey-white change in the peripheral retina visible without scleral indentation, with a well-defined posterior border, reflecting vitreoretinal adhesion/traction and outer retinal reflectance change.

location.notes: Between equator and ora, often temporal and in myopic or darkly pigmented eyes; may be large or migratory; its posterior border can be a site of tears.

drawing.description: Outline the white area in blue and cross-hatch it with blue lines.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (white with or without pressure: blue cross-lined)

name: White with pressure
definition: A grey-white opacification of the peripheral retina that appears only on scleral indentation, related to vitreoretinal adherence/peripheral retinal sclerosis.

location.notes: Between equator and ora, often bordering lattice, snail-track or retinoschisis; common in normal eyes.

drawing.description: Outline the area in blue and cross-hatch it with blue lines (same symbol as white without pressure; annotate 'WWP').

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (white with or without pressure: blue cross-lined)

name: Dark without pressure
definition: A flat, well-demarcated area of darker brown-grey fundus in the mid-periphery or periphery, visible without indentation, corresponding to reduced outer-segment/ellipsoid zone reflectance; benign and sometimes changes over time.

location.notes: Mid-periphery to periphery, often inferior or temporal; geographic, sometimes curvilinear.

drawing.description: Outline the darker area with a brown line (no fill) and annotate 'DWP'.

color_source: inferred: CMS brown = darker pigmentation seen through attached retina

name: Paving-stone (cobblestone) degeneration
definition: Discrete round yellow-white areas of peripheral chorioretinal atrophy with loss of RPE and choriocapillaris, pigmented borders and visible large choroidal vessels/sclera, that may coalesce into bands.

location.notes: Between equator and ora, most often inferiorly; usually bilateral; not associated with retinal detachment risk.

typical_size: individual lesions ~1/10–1 DD; may coalesce into bands

drawing.description: Draw small round lesions with black outlines and red cross-hatching inside, grouped or coalescent between equator and ora.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (black outline cross-hatched red = paving-stone degeneration of attached retina)

name: Paving-stone degeneration seen through detached retina
definition: Paving-stone chorioretinal atrophy viewed through overlying detached neurosensory retina.

location.notes: Within an area of retinal detachment between equator and ora.

drawing.description: Draw the lesions with brown outlines and red cross-hatching inside, within the blue detached area.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (brown outline cross-hatched red = paving-stone seen through detached retina)

name: Typical peripheral cystoid degeneration
definition: Clusters of tiny intraretinal cystoid spaces in the outer plexiform/inner nuclear layers immediately posterior to the ora serrata, giving a stippled grey-white honeycomb appearance; present in virtually all adults.

location.notes: Continuous band just posterior to the ora serrata, often 360°, most prominent temporally; precursor of typical degenerative retinoschisis.

typical_size: band ~1–2 DD (up to ~3 mm) wide posterior to the ora

drawing.description: Draw a band of small blue circles/stipple just posterior to the ora circle.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (cystoid degeneration: blue stippled/circled)

name: Reticular peripheral cystoid degeneration
definition: Cystoid spaces in the nerve fibre layer arranged in a fine reticular pattern that follows retinal vessels, located posterior to and continuous with typical cystoid degeneration; precursor of reticular retinoschisis.

location.notes: Posterior to the band of typical cystoid degeneration, between it and the equator; found in about one-fifth of adults.

typical_size: narrow band; 1 to several clock hours

drawing.description: Draw fine blue stippling in a linear/reticular arrangement along the vessels, posterior to the typical cystoid band.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (cystoid degeneration: blue stippled/circled)

name: Retinal tuft (vitreoretinal tuft, unspecified)
definition: A small focal elevation of peripheral retina with gliosis produced by vitreous or zonular traction at a point of firm vitreoretinal adhesion; classified as non-cystic, cystic, or zonular traction tufts.

location.notes: Near the vitreous base: intrabasal (zonular traction tufts), juxtabasal or extrabasal (cystic tufts).

drawing.description: Draw a small cluster of short blue lines at the site of the tuft.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (short blue lines = retinal tufts)

name: Cystic retinal tuft
definition: A congenital, small, elevated, chalky-white nodular lesion with cystic internal structure and often pigment at its base, with firm vitreoretinal adhesion that can produce a flap or operculated tear during posterior vitreous detachment.

location.notes: Equatorial to peripheral retina, posterior to the vitreous base (extrabasal/juxtabasal); present in ~5% of autopsy eyes.

drawing.description: Draw a small cluster of short blue lines; add black dots around it if pigment is present at the base.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (short blue lines = retinal tufts)

name: Non-cystic retinal tuft
definition: A short, thin, non-cystic projection of glial tissue from the retinal surface into the vitreous within the vitreous base, with negligible risk of retinal detachment.

location.notes: Within the vitreous base, just posterior to the ora; often multiple.

drawing.description: Draw one or a few very short blue lines near the ora.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (short blue lines = retinal tufts)

name: Zonular traction tuft
definition: A tuft of peripheral retina within the vitreous base pulled anteriorly by an aberrant zonular fibre that extends from the ciliary body to the apex of the tuft, occasionally causing a small hole or tear.

location.notes: Within the vitreous base near the ora, usually nasal (often inferonasal); usually single and unilateral; tuft points anteriorly toward the ciliary processes.

drawing.description: Draw a short blue line at the ora pointing anteriorly across the pars plana band toward the ciliary processes.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (short blue lines = retinal tufts)

name: Meridional fold
definition: A small radially oriented fold of redundant peripheral retina extending posteriorly from the ora, usually aligned with a dentate process, sometimes with a small hole at its posterior end.

location.notes: Radial, starting at the ora; most common superonasally and often bilateral/mirror-image.

drawing.description: Draw a single short blue line perpendicular to the ora circle, extending posteriorly from it.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (short blue lines = meridional folds)

name: Meridional complex
synonyms: dentate process aligned with ciliary process
definition: A meridional fold in which the dentate process (and associated fold) is in radial alignment with a ciliary process, forming a continuous radial ridge from retina across the pars plana.

location.notes: Radial, spanning from just posterior to the ora across the pars plana to a ciliary process; most common nasally.

drawing.description: Draw a short radial blue line crossing the ora circle and pars plana band to reach the ciliary-process circle.

color_source: inferred: CMS short blue lines = meridional folds

pubmed.title: Meridional folds, meridional complexes, and associated abnormalities of the peripheral retina.

name: Enclosed oral bay
synonyms: enclosed bay of the ora serrata
definition: A small oval island of pars plana epithelium completely surrounded by retina just posterior to the ora, formed by fusion of adjacent dentate processes; retinal tears may occur at its posterior margin.

location.notes: Immediately posterior to the ora serrata, more often nasally where dentate processes are prominent.

drawing.description: Draw a small closed oval loop attached to the posterior side of the ora circle, outlined in brown (pars plana tissue).

color_source: inferred: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology brown = uveal/pars plana tissue

name: Ora serrata pearl
definition: A glistening, white-yellow, drusen-like nodule on a dentate process at the ora serrata.

location.notes: On the dentate processes at the ora; often multiple.

drawing.description: Draw small solid green dots on the ora circle.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (pearls of ora: green solid)

name: Pars plana cyst
definition: A clear, dome-shaped cyst of the non-pigmented ciliary epithelium of the pars plana, between the ora serrata and the ciliary processes.

location.notes: In the pars plana band, more often temporally; may be multiple; can rarely detach into the vitreous.

drawing.description: Draw small brown-outlined circles or ovals within the pars plana band.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (pars plana cysts: brown solid)

name: Reticular (peripheral) pigmentary degeneration
synonyms: reticular degeneration of the pigment epithelium
definition: An age-related, net-like (polygonal) pattern of perivascular hyperpigmentation of the RPE in the peripheral fundus, associated with ageing and age-related macular degeneration.

location.notes: Equator to ora, often a 360° band; bilateral.

drawing.description: Draw a fine brown polygonal (net-like) pattern in the peripheral band without an outline.

color_source: inferred: CMS brown = RPE pigmentation seen through attached retina

pubmed.title: Reticular degeneration of the pigment epithelium.
Visualisation of peripheral retinal degenerations and anomalies with ocular imaging.

name: Peripheral pigment clumping / hyperpigmentation
definition: Focal clumps of RPE hyperplasia or migrated pigment in the peripheral retina, seen through attached retina.

location.notes: Anywhere in the periphery; often at margins of lattice, paving stone, old scars or demarcation lines.

drawing.description: Draw brown dots/clumps (black is used by some textbooks for intraretinal pigment).

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (brown = RPE or choroidal pigmentation seen through attached retina)

pubmed.title: Prevalence of peripheral retinal findings in retinal patients using ultra-widefield pseudocolor fundus imaging.

name: Peripheral chorioretinal atrophy
definition: A white to yellow-white area of peripheral loss of RPE and choriocapillaris with exposed choroidal vessels or sclera and pigmented margins, common in high myopia and hereditary vitreoretinopathies.

location.notes: Between equator and ora, often temporal; more frequent with increasing axial length.

drawing.description: Draw a patch with a black (pigmented) outline and leave the interior white; if large choroidal vessels are visible, use the paving-stone symbol (black outline, red cross-hatch).

color_source: inferred: brief textbook convention black = pigmented scars/borders; CMS paving-stone rule for visible choroidal vessels

Fundus Changes in High Myopia in Relation to Axial Length of the Globe.

name: Peripheral pigmented chorioretinal scar
definition: A healed, flat, sharply demarcated area of chorioretinal atrophy with heavy pigment clumping from prior inflammation, trauma or treatment.

location.notes: Anywhere in the periphery; retinal holes may form at the edge of chorioretinitis scars.

drawing.description: Draw a patch with a heavy black outline, black pigment clumps and a white (bare sclera) centre.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (black = hyperpigmentation from prior cryo/photocoagulation/diathermy and RPE pigment); brief textbook black = pigmented scars

name: Peripheral drusen
definition: Small yellow-white sub-RPE deposits located in the equatorial or peripheral fundus, common with age and age-related macular degeneration.

location.notes: Equator to periphery, often nasal or 360°.

drawing.description: Draw yellow stippling (dots) over the involved area.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (drusen: yellow stippled); brief textbook yellow = drusen

name: Snowflake degeneration
definition: Numerous discrete white-yellow crystalline or granular dots (about 100–200 µm) in the peripheral retina, either as an inherited snowflake vitreoretinal degeneration or overlying lattice, cystoid degeneration or retinoschisis.

location.notes: Near the equator and periphery, sometimes 360°, sometimes predominantly inferior; may coexist with white with/without pressure and lattice.

typical_size: each dot ~100–200 µm (≈1/10 DD); area 1 clock hour to 360°

drawing.description: Draw fine green stippling over the involved area.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (green stippled/dotted = frosting or snowflakes)

name: Typical degenerative (senile) retinoschisis
definition: Splitting of the peripheral neurosensory retina at the outer plexiform layer, arising from confluent typical cystoid degeneration, forming a smooth, immobile, shallow dome with a thin transparent inner wall, often with white flecks (snowflakes) and sheathed vessels.

location.notes: Bilateral and symmetric in many patients, inferotemporal most often, then superotemporal; extends from the ora posteriorly, posterior border frequently post-equatorial; produces an absolute scotoma.

drawing.description: Outline the schisis area in blue and cross-hatch it with blue lines (inner layer); draw inner-layer holes red cross-hatched and outer-layer holes red-filled, both with blue outlines.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (inner layer of retinoschisis: blue cross-lined); Requisites for Fundus drawing (SlideShare) https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retina-drwaing/163697941 (inner layer outlined and cross-hatched blue)

name: Reticular (bullous) degenerative retinoschisis
definition: Splitting of the peripheral retina at the nerve fibre layer, arising from reticular cystoid degeneration, forming a more elevated, bullous cavity with an extremely thin inner wall and a higher frequency of large outer-layer breaks.

location.notes: Inferotemporal most often; may extend posterior to the equator; outer-layer holes are typically large, round and posterior.

drawing.description: Outline in blue and cross-hatch in blue as for typical schisis; draw the larger outer-layer holes as red-filled with blue outlines.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (inner layer of retinoschisis: blue cross-lined); Requisites for Fundus drawing (SlideShare) https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/retina-drwaing/163697941

name: Schisis-detachment (retinoschisis-associated retinal detachment)
definition: A retinal detachment arising when schisis fluid passes through outer-layer breaks into the subretinal space, either localized and stable or progressive and symptomatic when combined with inner-layer breaks.

location.notes: Around outer-layer holes within or just beyond the schisis cavity, often posterior to the equator; localized forms are often bordered by a pigmented demarcation line.

drawing.description: Fill the detached area blue (outline blue), with the overlying schisis cross-hatched blue and outer-layer holes red-filled; add a black line for any pigmented demarcation line.

color_source: CMS L33567 App A (blue = detached retina); Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (black = pigmented demarcation lines)

name: X-linked retinoschisis (peripheral)
definition: Inherited (RS1) splitting of the inner retina which, peripherally, forms bullous schisis with very thin inner walls, large inner-layer holes, vitreous veils, silver-white spiculations and pigmentary change, usually with a coexisting spoke-wheel foveal schisis.

location.notes: Peripheral schisis most often inferotemporal; honeycomb appearance and pigmentary changes; associated with vitreous haemorrhage and retinal detachment.

typical_size: 1–2 quadrants; inner-layer holes may span several clock hours

drawing.description: Outline the schisis in blue and cross-hatch in blue; draw the large inner-layer holes with blue outline and red cross-hatching; draw vitreous veils in green with their red/blue vessels.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (inner layer of retinoschisis blue cross-lined; inner-layer holes red cross-lined; vitreous membranes green)

name: Vitreous veil (X-linked retinoschisis)
definition: A remnant of the extensively broken inner wall of X-linked retinoschisis that floats in the vitreous carrying retinal vessels.

location.notes: Overlying the area of peripheral schisis, suspended in the vitreous cavity; vessels within may bleed.

drawing.description: Draw a green-outlined membrane over the schisis area with red (artery) and blue (vein) vessel lines running through it.

color_source: Documentation & Drawing in Ophthalmology (eOphtha) https://www.eophtha.com/posts/documentation-drawing-in-ophthalmology (vitreous membranes: green); CMS L33567 App A (vessel colours)
